articles.title: From Tom Brady to Will Smith: How E1’s celebrity owners are shaping the future of electric boat racing
articles.summary: Tom Brady’s Team Brady has won the E1 World Championship for a third year in a row after a dramatic finish to the season in Miami.
articles.body: Tom Brady’s Team Brady has won the E1 World Championship for a third year in a row after a dramatic finish to the season in Miami. Pilots Emma Kimiläinen and Sam Coleman helped the team secure the title at the series’ first-ever double-header, held on Biscayne Bay on November 13 and 14. The result gives Brady’s team a place in the history of the all-electric powerboat series. But the Miami weekend also showed what E1 wants to become: a global sport that now brings racing, big names and a wider audience together around the world.Tom Brady, Emma Kimiläinen and Sam Coleman Lead E1’s Title-Winning TeamThe Miami finale was not a simple run to the trophy for Team Brady. The team finished last in Friday’s sixth round after struggling with speed and stability. That left the title fight open going into Saturday. The crew worked late to improve the boat, and the changes paid off.Team Brady reached the Race Off before moving into the finals. Coleman took the lead in Final 1, while Kimiläinen won Final 2. Their results helped the team finish the season with 198 points. Team Monaco came second with 145, followed by Will Smith’s Westbrook Racing on 141, according to the official E1 standings.The title was the third in a row for Brady’s team. It is also the third championship in E1 history, with Team Brady winning every season so far. Kimiläinen praised the team’s shared mindset and Brady’s support.Coleman pointed to a lesson Brady has shared with the team: win or lose, return to work on Monday. He said Brady’s experience with setbacks had taught the team to learn from a bad result rather than panic.Steve Aoki, LeBron James and Will Smith Bring Star Power as E1 Looks for New FansE1 is the first all-electric powerboat racing championship. It was created by Alejandro Agag, who also helped launch Formula E and Extreme E. Ten teams competed across seven rounds in 2026, with races in different parts of the world.The teams have well-known owners from sport and entertainment. Alongside Brady, they include LeBron James, Will Smith, Steve Aoki, Didier Drogba and Marc Anthony. Aoki, who was in Miami for the finale, told Daily Mail Sport he had not seen another sport with such a strong group of cultural figures behind it. He believes their reach can help E1 find viewers in many countries.The racing itself is different from what fans see on a track. Each team has one male and one female pilot, and they compete together rather than in separate categories. They take turns across qualifying and race stages in the same type of electric RaceBird boat. The boats are about 7.5 metres long and can reach around 60 mph. They lift slightly above the water, but rough waves can still make every turn difficult.E1 now wants to reach people who may not be drawn to its VIP Ocean Club, where guests watch races in a luxury setting. CEO Jamie Copas told Daily Mail Sport that the next step is to create fan zones at race locations. These would give more people a relaxed way to watch the action and learn about the series.Copas said wider attendance could also help E1 share its message about sustainability and men and women competing in the same championship. The Miami weekend gave Brady a third straight title. E1’s next challenge is to turn celebrity interest into a larger and more regular fan base.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Caitlin Clark and Trinity Rodman’s unexpected sporting connection makes their potential swap more interesting
articles.summary: Trinity Rodman believes a month-long sports swap with Caitlin Clark would be closer than people might expect.
articles.body: Trinity Rodman believes a month-long sports swap with Caitlin Clark would be closer than people might expect. The Washington Spirit forward shared her thoughts when she was asked who would handle the other's sport better. Rather than picking herself or Clark as the clear winner, the Olympic gold medalist predicted a close contest. Rodman also revealed that she had played basketball growing up and explained what kind of player she was. Her answer brought attention to an interesting part of both athletes' sporting backgrounds.Trinity Rodman Explains Why She Believes She Could Match Caitlin Clark in BasketballThe exchange happened on November 18 at the 2026 NWSL Awards ceremony at Lisner Auditorium at George Washington University in Washington, D.C. During a red-carpet interview, Rodman was asked how she and Clark would perform if they traded sports for an entire month.The 24-year-old forward did not think either player would have an easy advantage. She believed their performances could be quite similar because she had some experience playing basketball before choosing soccer as her main sport.“I think it would be pretty even, honestly. I used to play basketball too, so I feel like we would be, it’d be close,” Rodman said, according to Athlon Sports.She was then asked about her basketball skills and admitted that one part of her game needed work. Rodman explained that shooting was never her strong point, but she was comfortable handling the ball and attacking the basket.“I was a horrible shooter. I was a great dribbler. Going to the rim for sure,” she added.Her answer gave a better idea of why she expected a close contest. Rodman may not have been a strong shooter, but she had enjoyed playing basketball and understood some of the skills needed on the court.Caitlin Clark’s 42 High School Soccer Goals Give Trinity Rodman’s Prediction More WeightRodman's prediction also has an interesting connection to Clark's own sporting history. Before becoming one of the biggest names in women's basketball, the Indiana Fever guard played competitive high school soccer.At Dowling Catholic High School in West Des Moines, Iowa, Clark played as a varsity forward during the 2016-17 and 2017-18 seasons. According to her MaxPreps records, she scored 42 goals in 27 appearances across those two seasons.Her freshman year was particularly impressive. She scored 23 goals in 13 games before adding another 19 goals in 14 appearances as a sophomore. She also earned All-Iowa recognition as a freshman.Clark eventually decided to focus entirely on basketball. However, soccer remained an important part of her athletic development. In an April 2025 interview with David Letterman on Netflix, as reported by Sports Illustrated, she spoke about how playing soccer helped her understand passing angles and find teammates who were moving across the field.Rodman also had a genuine connection to basketball before making soccer her career. In a March 2022 interview with WBGO's SportsJam, she spoke about how her older brother, DJ, wanted her to play basketball with him.She explained that she enjoyed the competition, stealing the ball, shooting and scoring. However, soccer felt more natural to her.Both athletes have since reached the highest level in their chosen sports. Rodman earned her third NWSL Best XI selection on November 18 after previously receiving the honor in 2021 and 2024. The Washington Spirit credited her with 14 goals and 10 assists across 32 appearances in the 2026 regular season and playoffs. She was also a finalist for the league's MVP award, which went to North Carolina Courage forward Ashley Sanchez.Clark, meanwhile, finished the 2026 WNBA season with 22.3 points and 8.3 assists per game across 40 starts. According to the Indiana Fever, she earned her second All-WNBA First Team selection and became the only player in league history to finish a season among the top three in both scoring and assists.The two stars have clearly built their careers around different sports, but their earlier experiences make Rodman's prediction more interesting than a simple red-carpet answer.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Liz Cambage’s hidden struggles: Former WNBA star opens up about teenage drinking at 15 and depression
articles.summary: Liz Cambage was already making headlines in the WNBA at 19.
articles.body: Liz Cambage was already making headlines in the WNBA at 19. The Tulsa Shock had selected her with the second overall pick in 2011, and she became an All-Star in her rookie season. However, behind her success was a personal struggle that few people knew about. In a 2019 essay for The Players’ Tribune, Cambage spoke openly about her teenage drinking habits. She revealed that she had experienced blackouts from alcohol as young as 15 and first tried to become sober at just 18.In the essay titled DNP-Mental Health, published on August 11, 2019, Cambage asked whether people were truly ready to hear the difficult parts of her story.“Are people really ready to talk about how, starting at around 15 years old, I would just get blackout drunk some nights? Or that I’ve woken up with an IV in my arm, after a weekend of partying, not being able to remember a thing? Or that my first attempt at sobriety was at 18?” she wrote.Her words offered a different picture of a player who had achieved so much at such a young age. Cambage explained that people often say mental health matters, but that does not mean they are always ready to discuss the painful experiences behind it.She also spoke about spending almost every night of her rookie season alone and crying. At times, she locked herself inside her home for hours and avoided contact with other people.According to Basketball Network, alcohol had become a way for her to deal with difficult feelings. However, her own account in The Players’ Tribune showed that the problem was connected to much deeper struggles with anxiety and depression.Liz Cambage's Early WNBA Success Hid Her Personal StrugglesCambage's rise in basketball was quick. The Tulsa Shock selected her second overall in the 2011 WNBA Draft, behind Maya Moore. She averaged 11.5 points and 4.7 rebounds in her first season and earned an All-Star selection at just 19.She went on to become a four-time WNBA All-Star and earned two All-WNBA honors. In 2018, she won the league's scoring title while playing for the Dallas Wings. She also set a WNBA single-game scoring record with 53 points against the New York Liberty that year.However, her personal struggles continued alongside her basketball career.Cambage first stepped away from the WNBA in 2013 before returning with Dallas in 2018. She later played for the Las Vegas Aces and Los Angeles Sparks. In August 2022, she announced that she was leaving the league. She later continued playing overseas, including in Israel and China.Her experience also brings attention to the struggles other former basketball players have faced after leaving the game.Former WNBA player Leslie Johnson spoke about her battle with alcoholism in an interview with WRTV in 2025. She explained that drinking became her way of dealing with life after basketball.“I just put it all in the bottle,” Johnson said.She also shared that she had been sober for 13 years. Johnson now runs Hushed No More, an organization that works to raise mental health awareness among athletes. The group also joined local organizations for an event in Indianapolis ahead of the 2025 WNBA All-Star Weekend.Liz Cambage Questioned the WNBA's Approach to Mental HealthCambage's 2019 essay also raised questions about how professional basketball teams handle mental health.She wrote the piece after missing two games for the Las Vegas Aces in August 2019. The team listed her absences as "DNP-Rest." However, Cambage said the reason should have been recorded as "DNP-Mental Health."She explained that she wanted people to understand what was actually happening rather than give them a short answer to stop further questions.Cambage also compared depression to a rip current at a beach. She explained how someone can enjoy a normal day before slowly being pulled into deeper water without noticing what is happening.To her, that was what depression felt like.She also praised the NBA for requiring every team to have a mental health professional on its staff. However, she questioned why the WNBA did not have the same requirement.Cambage returned to action on August 9, 2019, against the Chicago Sky. She scored 28 points and grabbed 11 rebounds, but the Aces lost 87-84. Two days later, she recorded 21 points and 12 rebounds in an 89-81 win over the Connecticut Sun, according to the Associated Press.She ended her essay with a message about living with anxiety and depression. She made it clear that these struggles did not simply disappear and that it was okay to keep dealing with them.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Dylan Larkin Traded to Canadiens From Red Wings, Full Details on NHL Draft Picks Involved Revealed
articles.summary: Former Detroit Red Wings captain Dylan Larkin is heading to Montreal after successfully forcing a trade from his longtime team.
articles.body:
Former Detroit Red Wings captain Dylan Larkin is heading to Montreal after successfully forcing a trade from his longtime team.

The Montreal Canadiens are acquiring Larkin, a 2028 second-round pick and a 2027 third-round pick in exchange for Michael Hage, Kirby Dach, Samuel Montembeault and four draft picks.

The Athletic's Pierre LeBrun reported Larkin had been open to Montreal for more than two months:

Of note, Larkin is scheduled for two trips back to Detroit this season. His return will come on Thursday, Feb. 18, and the Canadiens will make another trip back to the Motor City on Saturday, March 20. Montreal will also host Detroit on Sunday, March 28.

The trade comes just more than a month after Habs fans let their desires be known:

Larkin will now join a Montreal squad that is in third place in the Atlantic, having gone 14-6-4 in its first 24 games. Its 32 points are tied with the Tampa Bay Lightning (15-6-2), who have only played in 23 games, however. Both clubs sit one point back of the Ottawa Senators (15-6-3, 33 points) for the top spot in the Atlantic.

Larkin, 30, is signed through 2030-31 on a contract worth $8.7 million per year, per PuckPedia .

He is coming out of five straight 30-goal seasons in Detroit, most recently posting 67 points (34 goals, 33 assists) in 74 games of the 2025-26 campaign.

Larkin could now slot in as a top-line center as Montreal looks to contend for a Stanley Cup next spring.

The Wings responded to Larkin's request for a trade this offseason by dismissing former general manager Steve Yzerman and stripping their former leader of his captaincy.

The Detroit Free Press ' Helene St. James initially reported Larkin, who holds a full no-trade clause through the next two seasons, had submitted a three-team trade list featuring only the Minnesota Wild, Florida Panthers and Vegas Golden Knights.

As of mid-October Larkin had expanded that list to include the Dallas Stars, Washington Capitals, Carolina Hurricanes, Utah Mammoth, Tampa Bay Lightning, New Jersey Devils and Colorado Avalanche, St. James reported.

Larkin has played 11 seasons for the Red Wings since the franchise selected him with the No. 15 pick of the 2014 draft.

A Red Wings team led by Henrik Zetterberg and Pavel Datsyuk made the playoffs during Larkin's rookie season, but Larkin hasn't been back to the postseason since.

Detroit has gotten close to the playoffs before falling short following an underwhelming finish to each of the last four seasons.

The Red Wings were most recently in a playoff spot at the end of February 2025 before going 5-7-2 in March and missing out on the postseason.

Larkin will now hope to get a chance to make his first playoff appearance since 2015, while the Red Wings will look to turn the page as the team tries to get out of the longest active postseason drought in the NHL.

Larkin, a Michigan native who played one season for the Wolverines, served as alternate captain for the Red Wings from 2018 until he was named captain in January 2021.

He departs from Detroit ranked 10th in Red Wings history with 278 goals and 649 points in 818 career games for the franchise. He had two goals and four assists in 10 games this season, having last played on October 26.

articles.title: Red Wings send Dylan Larkin to Canadiens in blockbuster trade, concluding dramatic saga
articles.summary: Larkin was suspended by Detroit on Oct. 29 after he told the team that he would not play for them while awaiting his trade request.
articles.body:
Another weeks-long NHL trade saga has come to an end, as the Detroit Red Wings traded Dylan Larkin to the Montreal Canadiens. The teams announced the deal on Sunday.

In return for Larkin, the Red Wings received forward Kirby Dach, goaltender Samuel Montembeault and the rights to forward Michael Hage (who is currently playing at University of Michigan). Detroit also received a quartet of draft picks, including conditional first-round picks for 2027 and 2029.

Montreal received a 2028 second-round draft pick and a 2027 third-rounder from the Red Wings, alongside Larkin.

Larkin departs Detroit after parts of 12 seasons with the team, which drafted him 15th overall in 2014. Tensions have been brewing between the former Detroit captain and his team for months after Larkin requested a trade over the summer.

Before the season, the Red Wings stripped Larkin of his captaincy , a role Larkin had held for the past six seasons. The tension escalated on Oct. 29, when Larkin told Detroit he would no longer play for the team while awaiting his trade. He was subsequently suspended by the team without pay.

The situation stayed in limbo over the following weeks, as the Red Wings continued to slip without their star forward. Detroit reportedly received offers by mid-November, but none matched the value that Larkin had to the team, per Detroit Free Press' Helene St. James .

Larkin, who was born and raised near Detroit and attended the University of Michigan for a year before being drafted by the Red Wings, quickly lost favor within his home state. Fans have booed him during home games throughout the season before his suspension.

In addition to losing goodwill, Larkin has also been losing money: The forward has forfeited $41,237 per day since being suspended. As of Nov. 21, Larkin has lost more than $1 million of his 2026-27 salary.

Larkin, who signed an eight-year, $69.6 million contract in 2023, has five years remaining on the deal. The contract included a no-trade clause, which led Larkin to give Detroit a list of locations to which he was willing to be traded.

Larkin's saga mirrored that of former Winnipeg Jets goaltender Connor Hellebuyck, his Team USA teammate. Hellebuyck was eventually shipped to the New Jersey Devils after a monthslong standoff. Unlike Hellebuyck, whose suspension began after he failed to show up for training camp, Larkin did initially arrive at the Red Wings' camp before deciding to sit out at the end of October.

Now, Larkin will join the Canadiens, adding a veteran presence to a young, talented roster. The Habs made it to the Eastern Conference Final last year, deeper in the postseason than any of the other Canadian teams as the country tries desperately to break its Stanley Cup drought. Montreal fell to the eventual champion Carolina Hurricanes

With the NHL season about a quarter done, the Habs are currently third in the competitive Atlantic Division.

articles.title: Broncos’ Sean Payton pulls off classy postgame move in honor of Tom Jackson
articles.summary: Coach Sean Payton’s Denver Broncos are 8-2 after a 38-24 home win over the Las Vegas Raiders that saw offensive coordinator Davis Webb’s unit come to life on...
articles.body:
Coach Sean Payton 's Denver Broncos are 8-2 after a 38-24 home win over the Las Vegas Raiders that saw offensive coordinator Davis Webb's unit come to life on a day when franchise star Tom Jackson's passing was announced, leading to a 'Jacked Up' ESPN tribute . The Broncos' offense starred in the win as Jonah Coleman reached a Clinton Portis pantheon at the running back position.

Following the game, Payton had a special tribute locked and loaded for Jackson.

"He got a game ball tonight, his family…Part of the rich history, obviously, tough loss for everyone," Payton said, clearly emotional over the loss of the Broncos and ESPN legend.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

Jackson was a big-time playmaker with the Broncos, intercepting 20 passes and recovering eight fumbles in 14 seasons with the franchise.

Denver's Vance Joseph-led defense didn't have its best day against the Raiders, giving up nearly 370 yards to its rookie Fernando Mendoza-led attack, but the offense picked them up. QB Bo Nix had 225 yards passing with one touchdown and one interception, while Coleman rushed for 111 yards on 24 carries with three touchdowns.

The Broncos missed out on key opportunities in the first half as Troy Franklin botched a Nix deep ball that had six points written all over it. The second half was better as the Broncos cashed in their opportunities, cruising to a much-needed division win.

Coach Payton and his franchise got the opportunity to learn about a true Broncos and NFL legend on Sunday, but not under the circumstances that they wanted to hear. The Broncos' division title hopes remain intact heading into Week 12 against the Steelers as fans continue to mourn Jackson's passing, and to remember his timeless contributions.

articles.title: No. 7 UCLA breezes past Delaware 85-48 to stay unbeaten
articles.summary: LOS ANGELES (AP) — Filip Jovic came off the bench to score 17 points in 19 minutes, and No. 7 UCLA rolled to an 85-48 victory over Delaware on Sunday.
articles.body:
LOS ANGELES (AP) — Filip Jovic came off the bench to score 17 points in 19 minutes, and No. 7 UCLA rolled to an 85-48 victory over Delaware on Sunday.

Jovic made 7 of 8 shots from the floor and 3 of 5 free throws for the Bruins (6-0), adding six rebounds and two assists.

Trent Perry made three 3-pointers and scored 15 for UCLA. Nikola Kusturica added 12 points, including the first six in a game-opening 8-2 run. Xavier Booker scored 10 and Eric Dailey Jr. totaled nine points and nine rebounds.

Joe Philon III followed his layup with a dunk to give UCLA its first double-digit lead at 29-19 and the Bruins finished on a 16-3 run for a 41-22 advantage at halftime. Jovic had 10 points at the break on 5-for-5 shooting.

UCLA upped its lead to 30 at 65-35 with 10 minutes remaining after Eric Dailey Jr. tipped in a miss to finish a 16-2 run.

Kachi Nzeh led the Blue Hens (4-3) with nine points.

UCLA shot 55% overall but made only 5 of 18 from 3-point range. The Bruins turned 22 Delaware turnovers into 27 points.

The Blue Hens shot 40% and went 5 for 19 from distance.

articles.title: Dylan Larkin trade grades: Who won Canadiens and Red Wings deal?
articles.summary: Dylan Larkin has been traded from the Red Wings to the Canadiens in a deal involving Kirby Dach, Samuel Montembeault, Michael Hage and so much more.
articles.body:
Our long national nightmare is over: Dylan Larkin -- the former Detroit Red Wings captain who had his "C" stripped after a trade request -- has finally been traded. And WHEW it's a biggie.

The Montreal Canadiens paid a large sum to acquire Larkin, but it makes sense as the team's Stanley Cup window continues to open up. They've got the scoring up front, some solid blue liners and a young stud goaltender in Jacob Fowler. Now? They add Larkin, the kind of leader and star forward a team looking for a Cup needs. But as you'll see, the Canadian franchise paid a lot for his services.

So who won this one? What are the details? As always, we're handing out grades for both sides:

Canadiens get: C Dylan Larkin, a 2028 second-round pick and a 2027 third-round pick

Red Wings get F Kirby Dach, G Sam Montembeault, F Michael Hage, a 2027 first-round pick, a 2027 second-round pick, a 2028 fourth-round pick and a 2029 first-round pick

WOW. WOWWWWWWWWWWWW. I love this move. Montembeault won 31 games last year but had a 3.43 GAA and a .872 save percentage this year, so the Wings might hope to see him rebound. Dach is a depth forward and Hage is the No. 2 prospect in the Montreal system per NHL.com after he was a 2024 first-rounder (and he's playing REALLY well for Michigan this year).

But let's talk about Larkin, who brings the intangibles, leadership and two-way play as a forward to a young team filled with talent that needed a player... well, like Larkin! It's a perfect fit. When you're poised to make the leap like the Canadiens seem to be, you shove all in like this. GRADE: A

I'm kind of shocked that Larkin -- who was clearly unhappy and everyone knew he was -- fetched this kind of return. But Detroit's front office should be very happy with what it got back: Some good picks, a potential future star in Hage and a change-of-scenery project in Montembeault.

Could they have gotten more NHL-ready talent here? Maybe that wasn't the goal. Ultimately, the Wings did well with what was a super dramatic situation. GRADE: B+

articles.title: Red Wings Fans React to Dylan Larkin Trade
articles.summary: Detroit Red Wings fans react to the blockbuster Dylan Larkin trade to Montreal, with mixed emotions about the return and their former captain.
articles.body:
The Dylan Larkin era in Detroit has officially come to an end , and Red Wings fans have plenty to say about the blockbuster trade that sent their former captain to the Montreal Canadiens.

Following Sunday's stunning announcement, social media erupted with reactions from fans across Hockeytown. Most were thrilled with the enormous return Detroit received, praising interim GM Shawn Horcoff for ripping off Montreal.

One thing is certain: This is a trade that Red Wings fans won't forget anytime soon.

Red Wings Fans React to Massive Trade Package

As part of the deal, Detroit received Michael Hage, Kirby Dach, Samuel Montembeault, two conditional first-round draft picks, a second-round pick, and a fourth-round pick, according to TSN . Montreal received Larkin along with Detroit's 2027 third-round pick and 2028 second-round selection.

It's an enormous package, and the potential arrival of Hage has generated considerable excitement among fans who have been following the young prospect's development.

For many supporters, this trade represents an opportunity for Detroit to reshape its roster and build toward the future. Others remain skeptical about parting ways with a hometown star who spent more than a decade wearing the Winged Wheel.

What Red Wings Fans Are Saying About the Dylan Larkin Trade

An Emotional Ending to the Dylan Larkin Era

Regardless of how fans feel about the return, Larkin's departure marks a significant moment in Red Wings history. The Waterford, Michigan native was selected 15th overall in the 2014 NHL Draft and eventually became the organization's captain.

For years, Larkin was expected to help lead Detroit back to Stanley Cup contention. Unfortunately, the Red Wings struggled to regain their place among the NHL's elite, and the relationship between Larkin and the organization eventually deteriorated.

After months of speculation surrounding his future , the two sides have now officially gone their separate ways.

Meanwhile, the Canadiens are adding an established NHL center to their lineup, while Detroit is betting that its collection of young players and draft capital will help accelerate the next chapter of the franchise.

The trade also means Larkin will remain in the Atlantic Division, setting up what should be some extremely interesting matchups between the Red Wings and Canadiens.

Detroit fans have already witnessed plenty of twists in the Larkin trade saga , but Sunday's announcement finally brought the uncertainty to an end.

Now comes the debate over whether Detroit received enough in return.

articles.title: Ravens Star Silenced for Joke, Even as Team’s Season Collapses
articles.summary: Marlon Humphrey made a joke on his own podcast. Asked what Baltimore is best at making, he named the Star-Spangled Banner and National Bohemian beer, then ad...
articles.body:
Marlon Humphrey made a joke on his own podcast. Asked what Baltimore is best at making, he named the Star-Spangled Banner and National Bohemian beer, then added, "They're best at making criminals." It was a throwaway line in a casual conversation. He immediately noted it would get cut. The next day, he apologized, pointing out that he's spent his whole career in the city, has welcomed a son there, and invests locally.

The Ravens treated it like a major offense. Coach Jesse Minter sent him home from the facility and made him a healthy scratch for Sunday's game against the Panthers. One-game deactivation, still gets paid, conversations "personal and private." Officially it's about removing a distraction while the team tries to snap a five-game losing streak.

That framing doesn't hold up. The Ravens are 4-6 and sliding. They're already missing other defensive starters. Humphrey has started every game this season and is the longest-tenured defensive player on the roster. His recent play has been inconsistent, yet the organization has kept him in the lineup and at the top of the cornerback pay scale. A light podcast joke produced an immediate benching . The actual losses have not.

Mayor Brandon Scott and others called the comment unacceptable and the apology insufficient. Public criticism is part of the job. What's harder to defend is a struggling franchise choosing this moment for a public stand. When a team is getting beaten week after week, deactivating a starter over an offhand remark looks more like virtue signaling than football discipline. It signals seriousness without fixing the problems that actually cost games.

Humphrey is expected back next week. The Ravens' larger issues—offensive inconsistency, defensive holes, a losing streak—will still be there. Silencing a player for a joke doesn't change any of that. It just gives a flailing organization something to point to while the losses continue.

articles.title: Best Week 12 waiver wire pickups after the Sunday early slate
articles.summary: Justice Hill, Ted Hurst, and Caleb Douglas highlight the top early waiver wire fantasy football targets entering Week 12.
articles.body:
The early games of Week 11 are winding down. It wasn't the prettiest slate of games, but football games and stats were produced on a field with grass or some kind of turf covering that field. We've seen some ugly football today, but as teams lose players to injuries and start young players for evaluation, things get ugly.

Mendoza complete under 50% of his passes against the Broncos in Denver, but he also put up 267 yards three touchdowns and a pick-six to end the game. Three touchdown passes is pretty good, especially when you consider that Brock Bowers was unable to play.

How useful he'll be in fantasy moving forward is hard to know, but he's proving he can put up fantasy points with some average receivers. Getting Bowers back will be huge and having Ashton Jeanty breaking off huge catch and runs doesn't hurt either.

Smith completed 17-of-21 passes for 176 yards and three touchdowns in Sunday's 27-24 win over the Chargers. He remains a streaming option at quarterback despite inconsistency. Next week he faces the Dolphins, who he put up 287 yards and three touchdowns against in Week 7.

Dike took over the slot role in Week 11 and ended up leading the team in receptions and yards, catching 6-of-7 targets for 69 yards. It wasn't a huge fantasy game, but if he can keep that slot job, he should be set up for a good PPR floor moving forward.

Fernando Mendoza appears to like wide receiver Jack Bech, as he's targeted him on 25% of his passes through his first two games. This week Bech caught 8-of-9 targets for88 yards and a touchdown. This usage comes with Brock Bowers off the field for most of the time, but I do like that Mendoza likes him and if that keeps up next week with Bowers possibly back, we may be onto something.

With Jacoby Brissett in as the Ravens quarterback, they are going to chuck the ball to finish out the season. In his two starts he's thrown the ball 49 and 37 times. This isn't your Lamar Jackson Ravens anymore, as he attempted 20, 20, 31, and 25 passes in his four full starts this year. Derrick Henry needs the threat of Jackson taking off as a runner to keep teams honest. Without that the Ravens aren't going to force the run like they once did.

More passing is great for Zay Flowers and good for Brissett and running back Justice Hill. This week against the Panthers, Brissett completed 24-of-37 passes for 276 yards, one touchdown and one interception, while running twice for seven yards. That's not winning your league for you, but there is no-doubt upside there if you need help at QB.

Derrick Henry had a good game against the Panthers, rushing 13 times for 94 yards and a touchdown, while catching four passes for 17 yards. Unfortunately he lost a fumble after one of those receptions and he appeared to have suffered a concussion late in the game on his 15-yard touchdown run. That could set up more touches for passing down back Hill next week against the Texans. This week he played well, rushing six times for 69 yards and a touchdown, while catching 4-of-5 targets for 27 yards. He also lost a fumble in the back of the end zone. He was so close to two touchdowns on the day.

Even if Henry doesn't miss time, Hill is worth a pickup in this more pass oriented offense moving forward.

Baker Mayfield and the Buccaneers were finally forced to throw the ball, and it didn't go great, as they lost to the Lions, but that was likely. The good news is that Mayfield and company were able to put up some fantasy points through the air. The leader of the group ended up being Hurst, who led the team in targets, receptions, yards and touchdowns. He caught 5-of-7 targets for 56 yards and a pair of touchdowns. We've seen Hurst show out in the past, but this looks like we could see him take over as WR1 if he can stay healthy. The Bucs really need someone to step up in the receiving game, and I like Hurst's chances.

Kyle McCord is not good. But, he is still targeting Douglas like a No. 1 wide receiver. This week he threw in his general direction 10 times, but only completed two passes for 30 yards to the rookie. The looks are there, but the connection isn't. Next week the Dolphins get the Jets, who Douglas caught two touchdowns against last time they met in Week 7. If you are in a matchup next week that doesn't look good for your team, get Douglas into your lineup for a shot at some offensive fireworks.

articles.title: Let fans dream: we're happy, but chasing our dream - Gabriel Milito
articles.summary: Chivas put the icing on the cake of their Apertura 2026 regular season: they beat Cruz Azul, seized first place overall with 33 points, finished with the tou...
articles.body:
Chivas put the icing on the cake of their Apertura 2026 regular season: they beat Cruz Azul, seized first place overall with 33 points, finished with the tournament's best home record, and now await their quarterfinal series against Pachuca. The support of the Red-and-White Nation was crucial to securing their sixth home win, as the Chivas faithful never stopped cheering on Guadalajara for a single second.

To overcome La Máquina, the Flock showed the solidity they aim to replicate in their first playoff tie, as Gabriel Milito noted in his post-match press conference. The Chivas coach encouraged the Red-and-White Republic to dream alongside the team as they pursue their ultimate goal.

"We finished the regular season very well, winning and taking the opportunity to finish top, which is what we wanted. A new tournament begins, and we all start from zero."

"We have a tough series against Pachuca, a good team. We'll stay humble as always, looking to compete and play our game, as the team has been doing for some time."

"In these kinds of matches, a bad 10–15 minutes can put your chances of advancing at risk; we'll try to get as close to perfection as possible. We have to work hard and earn our place in the next round."

"It's important to have that sense of belonging to the club, as this squad does. Those of us who arrived later are all proud to represent Chivas , and our goal is very clear."

"We know achieving that ultimate goal is no easy task, but we have to keep the dream alive and see how far we can go. Now we have to think solely and exclusively about Pachuca. Today was good; finishing first deserves a lot of credit given everything we went through during the season."

"Hopefully, we can be at our very best for what comes next, which is decisive. The series will demand that of us. The players know how important it is to push ourselves to our limits, both individually and collectively."

"It was important because it was the end of the regular season, and victory would give us not just three points but first place. Now a new tournament begins with no clear favorite; that will have to be proven once each match gets underway."

"We're happy, but we haven't achieved what we're striving for."

"Let the fans dream. They'll keep supporting the team because they see that we give everything, and we bring that competitive spirit we already have to every match. We have to dream. We're going into this series to let our performances show what we're capable of."

"Without humility, effort, and the right mentality, you achieve nothing in football. Those are our values, but we have to put them into practice. It will be a difficult series, but one thing is guaranteed: we'll give it absolutely everything."

"It's important to finish with the best defensive record and more points than everyone else. If there's one thing we've talked about, it's being solid and clinical. That's the ideal combination, and we'll try to achieve it in these playoffs."

"There are no easy matches in the Mexican league; we've seen that many times. We don't want any surprises. We have to stay focused, which is why I spoke about the team's maturity and the impression we're giving."

articles.title: Beede’s Breakdown: Magic fall flat, trail entire night in loss at Wizards
articles.summary: The Magic fell behind by as many as 25 points and never led against the Wizards on Sunday night to go 1-1 on their two-game weekend trip. With all five membe...
articles.body:
The Magic fell behind by as many as 25 points and never led against the Wizards on Sunday night to go 1-1 on their two-game weekend trip.

With all five members of its starting lineup finishing in double figures, including five-time All-NBA big man Anthony Davis (22 points), Washington cruised to its third consecutive victory, 116-96, over Orlando inside Capital One Arena.

The Magic had a hard time keeping up with the Wizards from distance, an area of the court where Washington knocked down 56% of its 3-point shots and held Orlando to just 31% shooting on the other end.

It's the second win for Washington over Orlando this month. The Magic lost to the Wizards by nine points at home on Nov. 2, and the sides will face each other a third time in November on Saturday. The sides won't see each other again until much later in the season on April 3 for their fourth and final regular-season meeting as Southeast Division opponents.

Washington (7-11) did a solid job slowing down Magic forward Franz Wagner, who had scored 30-plus points in five of the past seven games. Wagner was limited to 16 points in the loss while teammate Jalen Suggs missed all six of his 3-point attempts to score just nine points in 22 minutes of action.

The Magic (7-9) will look to regroup at home when they host the Pistons in a big NBA Cup game on Tuesday night at Kia Center.

The Magic lacked a sense of urgency when the Wizards scored the first 11 points of the game. It took three minutes of action for Orlando to get on the board after back-to-back layups from Wagner.

Washington had success pushing the ball in transition and from beyond the arc in the opening frame. The Wizards held an 11-0 advantage in fast break points and shot 6-for-11 from 3-point by the end of the first quarter.

Meanwhile, the Magic went 3-for-14 from distance in the first quarter and were outrebounded 15-7 to fall behind by 17 points, 38-21, after the opening 12 minutes of the game.

Washington entered Sunday's game shooting 31.9% from beyond the arc, which marked the third-worst 3-point percentage in the league.

But against the Magic, the Wizards could hardly miss from distance.

Orlando often failed to closeout on defense to open shooters on the perimeter and the Wizards made them pay for the disfunction. Through three quarters alone, Washington tied its season-high for 3-pointers made in a game with 18.

The Wizards finished 22-for-39 from 3-point range and had seven different players hit from distance, including guard Bilal Coulibaly who made four. Coulibaly had made a total of six 3-pointers in his first 16 games played this season.

On the other end of the floor, the Magic finished 12-for-39 from 3-point range with both reserves Nikola Vucevic and Jevon Carter both shooting 1-for-4 on the perimeter. Desmond Bane (17 points) shot 3-for-8 from 3 in 33 minutes.

One of the few bright spots for the Magic on Sunday night was the play of third-year forward Tristan da Silva.

After scoring just six points at Brooklyn on Friday night, da Silva bounced back in a major way with 18 points in 27 minutes off the bench.

Da Silva knocked down a team-high four 3-pointers when he shot 6-for-10 from the field and added three rebounds.

Jason Beede can be reached at jbeede@orlandosentinel.com

articles.title: Coaches Poll Delivers Encouraging Sign for SEC Ahead of Rivalry Week
articles.summary: ATHENS, Ga. — College football’s coaches have weighed in, and their latest rankings provide another encouraging development for the Southeastern Conference....
articles.body:
ATHENS, Ga. — College football's coaches have weighed in, and their latest rankings provide another encouraging development for the Southeastern Conference.

Georgia maintained the No. 1 position in Sunday's US LBM Coaches Poll following its 34-6 victory over South Carolina.

However, the Bulldogs were hardly the only SEC program making noise.

Alabama, Texas and Tennessee climbed in the rankings, while Oklahoma and Missouri returned to the top 25.

As a result, nine SEC teams enter Rivalry Week ranked by the coaches.

Georgia (10-1) received 60 first-place votes, keeping the Bulldogs ahead of undefeated Utah and one-loss Notre Dame.

The Bulldogs have now won four consecutive games, including decisive victories over Ole Miss, Missouri and South Carolina.

Meanwhile, Alabama climbed from No. 7 to No. 5, Texas advanced from No. 8 to No. 6 and Tennessee moved from No. 9 to No. 7.

Those improvements matter as the conference prepares to determine Georgia's opponent in Atlanta.

Although the coaches poll does not control playoff selections, the rankings reflect the national perception of teams entering the regular season's final stretch.

One notable difference separates the polls

The coaches ranked Alabama fifth, one position ahead of Texas. The AP poll reversed that order, placing Texas fifth and Alabama sixth.

Additionally, Kentucky remained in the coaches poll at No. 25 despite dropping out of the AP rankings.

Ohio State experienced the opposite situation, falling out of the coaches poll while remaining No. 25 in the AP Top 25.

These differences demonstrate how closely voters are evaluating programs with similar records.

More importantly, the SEC's leading teams still have opportunities to influence their postseason positions.

Alabama hosts Auburn in the Iron Bowl, Texas visits Texas A&M and Tennessee travels to Vanderbilt.

Meanwhile, Georgia closes its regular season against Georgia Tech.

The coaches have delivered their latest assessment. Now, the SEC's biggest rivals get the opportunity to answer on the field.

articles.title: Red Wings Deal The MN Wild Trade Target to Canada
articles.summary: The Minnesota Wild's long pursuit of a top center ended Sunday night when the Detroit Red Wings traded Dylan Larkin to Montreal.
articles.body:
Dylan Larkin hasn't played a game for the Detroit Red Wings since Oct. 26 against Edmonton. But the Minnesota Wild have been chasing him since the 30-year-old center asked for a trade going all the way back to June.

In fact, Minnesota was on his original three-team trade list, and the only team league-wide that stayed in it from start to finish. Unfortunately, all that effort went for naught on Sunday evening when news broke that the Team USA Olympic gold medalist has finally accepted a trade to the one place he's been trying to avoid for months.

Red Wings trade Dylan Larkin to Montreal, not the MN Wild

Dylan Larkin has been traded to the Montreal Canadiens for two players, a prospect's rights and four draft picks. Larkin accepted his fate after forfeiting more than $1 million in salary due to suspension.

The Canadiens have acquired forward Dylan Larkin, Detroit's second-round pick in 2028 and third-round pick in 2027 in exchange for forward Kirby Dach, goaltender Samuel Montembeault, the rights to forward Michael Hage, a first-round pick in 2027, a second-round pick in 2027, a fourth-round pick in 2028 and a first-round pick in 2029. #GoHabsGo — Canadiens Montréal (@CanadiensMTL) November 22, 2026

The Canadiens have acquired forward Dylan Larkin, Detroit's second-round pick in 2028 and third-round pick in 2027 in exchange for forward Kirby Dach, goaltender Samuel Montembeault, the rights to forward Michael Hage, a first-round pick in 2027, a second-round pick in 2027, a fourth-round pick in 2028 and a first-round pick in 2029. #GoHabsGo

Canadiens Montréal (@CanadiensMTL) November 22, 2026

Both teams announced the trade around 7:45 p.m. Central. Detroit gets forward Kirby Dach, goaltender Samuel Montembeault and the rights to prospect Michael Hage, plus first-round picks in 2027 and 2029, a 2027 second-round pick and a 2028 fourth-round pick. Montreal also gets Detroit's second-round pick in 2028 and third-round pick in 2027. Neither team announced any retained salary.

David Pagnotta ( The Fourth Period ) said Sunday night that the Canadiens had started warming up to moving Hage a few weeks ago, but Larkin wouldn't waive for Montreal at the time. Michael Russo ( The Athletic ) said a Wild source had already told him the Canadiens would get Larkin by the end of the week.

Obviously, the Minnesota Wild have proven early this season (with a 17-3-5 start) that they do not need Dylan Larkin to win hockey games. However, you can bet Bill Guerin will be on the phone this week trying to devise a plan to get the Central Division leader over the top, come playoffs.

Meanwhile, Montreal gets a center who led Detroit's forwards in average ice time at 21:41 this season, with 2 goals, 4 assists and a plus-3 in 10 games. Larkin has 278 goals and 649 points in 818 career games , all with the Red Wings, which ranks 10th in franchise history in both.

He is also signed through 2030-31 on the eight-year extension he signed in March 2023, which carries an $8.7 million cap hit. The Canadiens are 14-6-4 and third in the Atlantic Division, while the Red Wings sit seventh in the Atlantic at 8-12-3.

articles.title: 49ers starting lineman carted off after brutal injury vs. Vikings
articles.summary: The 49ers met the Vikings on Sunday in Mexico, and while things were going well early, they lost a big part of their offense in the second quarter.
articles.body:
The San Francisco 49ers were enjoying a 14-10 lead over the Minnesota Vikings in the second quarter of their international matchup in Mexico on Sunday night, but things took a sharp turn with about seven minutes to go until halftime

On a first-and-10 run by Christian McCaffrey, 49ers right tackle Colton McKivitz suffered a gruesome looking injury. His teammates were distraught after the play, and the veteran had to be carted off the field.

McKivitz played 100% of the snaps through the first 10 weeks of the season and through all 17 games in 2025. He also played 98% in both 2023 and 2024, so that speaks to the unfamiliar poisition the 49ers will find themselves in without him.

Vederian Lowe, who San Francisco signed to a one-year deal this offseason, entered the game in his place, and he'll have a very important role to play through the rest of this game and probably for a while for the 49ers.

articles.title: Hamlin Pointed to Brent Crews for the No. 11. Crews Says 12 Top 5s Aren’t Enough
articles.summary: Brent Crews says taking over Denny Hamlin's No. 11 at Joe Gibbs Racing would be a dream come true, but he knows he has to win more to earn it.
articles.body:
Brent Crews , the Joe Gibbs Racing driver Denny Hamlin pointed to as his likely replacement in June, says he hasn't been promised Hamlin's No. 11 Toyota.

Crews was asked on SiriusXM NASCAR Radio this week whether anyone has told him the No. 11 will be his. The seat means more to him than most: Hamlin was his favorite driver growing up, because 11 is his favorite number.

Crews Says His Rookie Numbers Aren't Enough Yet

Crews has just finished his rookie season in the O'Reilly Auto Parts Series, where he won Rookie of the Year. In 29 starts, he had 12 top-five finishes and 18 top-10s, but no wins, and finished 13th in points. He said those numbers don't make him a Cup Series driver yet.

"That would be a dream come true, truthfully. But nothing is promised. Just like when you guys are reading off my stat list, 12 top 5s and 18 top 10s is not what it takes to be a Cup Series driver, and I'm fully aware of that… Then I need to go out there, and I need to win a ton of races and perform at a high level and execute. And I know that, and I'm aware of that, and that's not really a pressure thing.

"I treat it as a privilege that I'm able to have this opportunity with this amazing race team to even be in the talks to be able to do that. So it's a blessing, and it's an amazing opportunity. And we're gonna give it all we got next year to go show them that it's us," Crews said.

Hamlin's Exit Depends on JGR's Next Driver

Hamlin first named Crews as his likely replacement in June, when he was asked about his future at JGR.

"I don't want to leave them in flux. They've got a great driver in Brent Crews that's gonna be ready more than likely by the end of next year," Hamlin said at the time.

Hamlin still plans to make 2027 his final full-time Cup season. On SiriusXM NASCAR Radio on Nov. 18, he said Joe Gibbs is already making house calls to talk him into racing longer, and that his decision will depend in part on whether JGR has its next driver ready.

"I want to make sure that they've got their next driver planned, lined up, all that stuff. I definitely am going to do whatever is best for Joe Gibbs Racing, but I'm not going to compromise my performance," Hamlin said.

Hamlin has also said he won't keep racing if he can't win every weekend. He turned 46 on Nov. 18 and finished third in the 2026 Cup standings, 56 points behind champion Kyle Larson, after winning four races. Crews, meanwhile, plans to spend next season proving he belongs in the conversation.

articles.title: Instant Analysis: Dak delivers 5 TDs; issues follow D in Cowboys win
articles.summary: The Cowboys offense scored on their first 8 drives, including 6 straight TDs in a big win over Tennessee. The defense showed some improvement.
articles.body:
The Cowboys have acted as a get-right team for several of their opponents this season. On Sunday's visit to AT&T Stadium, it was the Titans ' turn to step into the role for the Cowboys. By the time the final gun sounded, the Cowboys had put together their most compete outing of 2026, notching a much-needed 51-30 win to cap off a tumultuous week and keep the team's faint postseason hopes alive.

Quarterback Dak Prescott turned in one of his best days as a pro, CeeDee Lamb added to his video-game numbers in what is turning into another All-Pro season, and George Pickens posted his second straight 100-yard game as the offense scored on eight straight drives and ended with a Landry Shift.

But it was the defense that was under the microscope, in the play-calling debut of Mike Pettine and following the midweek demotion of Christian Parker. While the unit showed signs of improvement, many of the familiar issues of this season seemed to have followed the Cowboys, even through Sunday's decisive win.

The Titans are, to be blunt, one of the worst teams in the NFL this season. So any proclamations that the Cowboys have somehow miraculously turned things around would be premature at best. But maybe Sunday's victory was a start.

The Cowboys offense found the end zone four times on four possessions, the first time that's happened in over four calendar years. Prescott went 16-for-20 through the air, posting 182 yards and a pair of touchdowns en route to a 137.9 passer rating in the first half. Lamb continued his monster season, catching nine balls on 10 targets and going into the break with 103 yards and a touchdown.

The rushing attack added two scores, one from Javonte Williams and another from KaVontae Turpin. That 5.3-yards-per-carry average might have suggested that Brian Schottenheimer keep the ball on the ground after the team's opening-drive touchdown. Though a Titans penalty allowed the Cowboys to try a two-point play from the 1-yard-line, Dallas opted to throw into the end zone. The subsequent incompletion cost the Cowboys a point (assuming Brandon Aubrey would have connected on the PAT), but that proved to be the only legitimate complaint for Cowboys fans over the game's first 30 minutes.

That's because the defense, under newly-installed play-caller Pettine, looked more like the unit that had been expected to show up after the offseason reboot. The Cowboys allowed just 102 yards by Tennessee, sacked Cam Ward three times, logged five tackles for loss, stopped four of six third-down tries... and most important, gave up zero touchdowns going into intermission.

As has been the case in multiple games this season, though, things for the Cowboys in the second half didn't follow the same script, as a couple of longstanding bugaboos returned to haunt the Dallas defense. With the their first possession of the third quarter, the Titans drove the length of the field in a hurry. The majority of the damage- 38 free yards- came on a pass interference call on rookie Caleb Downs. When Ward took it into the end zone himself on the next snap to narrow the Cowboys' lead to 11 points, memories of Week 8's second-half collapse versus Arizona came flooding back for many.

Adding to those fears? The midweek redistribution of defensive coaching duties weren't enough to completely eliminate Dallas's propensity for giving up explosive plays. On the Titans' next possession, a total of four Cowboys defenders failed to touch wideout Carnell Tate while he was sitting on the ground after a reception; Tate got up and took the ball another 49 yards for a gut-punch score. It marked the 18th consecutive game in which the Dallas defense allowed 20 points or more. The Pettine/Parker defense certainly had its best showing of the season on Sunday, but one egregious mental error like that could easily cost this team their razor-thin playoff hopes if it hits during their December gauntlet of playoff-caliber opponents.

It was only the offense's pedal-to-the-metal execution that kept the Tennessee rally under wraps on Sunday. Prescott & Co. picked up where they left off, converting another two drives into touchdowns, making it six in a row to start this game. (That's the most to start a contest since 1993, which is as far back as the stat can be tracked by the Cowboys PR team.)

But Prescott wasn't done. Though a 49-yard field goal by Aubrey ended the Cowboys' touchdown streak, a short scoring pass to Brevyn Spann-Ford capitalized on a fumble recovery to give Prescott his fourth on the day. That capped Prescott's huge day at 28-of-33 for 325 yards. The performance ranks among Prescott's eight most accurate days, and the 147.3 final passer rating was Prescott's fourth-best outing as a pro. (He also added a touchdown run, his second of the season.)

In all, the Cowboys scored on eight straight drives Sunday, the only outlier coming on the final possession of the afternoon, which consisted of a lone kneeldown.

Despite the big win, the defense still has work to do. Only once this season have the 1-9 Titans topped the 30 points and 346 yards the Cowboys allowed on Sunday. While the third-down numbers were good (3 of 10), Dallas did let Tennessee convert both of their fourth-down tries on the day.

There will also be injury questions going into the short Thanksgiving Week; Cobie Durant took a nasty hit to the head, totally unnecessary friendly fire from teammate DeMarvion Overshown that came as the play was already ending. Safety Alijah Clark was also hurt, possibly thinning out the Cowboys secondary even further.

Expect penalties to also be addressed by the coaching staff. Another 11 flags for 128 yards give the Cowboys 90 accepted penalties on the season and over 800 yards walked off against them.

But for now, the Cowboys can celebrate their best game of 2026 and getting to within one game of .500, with a chance to notch back-to-back wins in front of a nationwide audience on Thanksgiving Day.

Pittsburgh Steelers wide receiver DK Metcalf was disqualified in the third quarter of Sunday's 19-16 loss to the Philadelphia Eagles after drawing his second personal foul of the game.

The sequence began earlier when Metcalf got into a shoving match with Eagles cornerback Cooper DeJean and was flagged for unnecessary roughness. Later in the quarter, after an incomplete pass, Metcalf and DeJean tangled again away from the play. Replays showed Metcalf reaching through DeJean's facemask and appearing to poke him in the eye area. Officials called unsportsmanlike conduct. Because it was Metcalf's second such penalty, he was automatically ejected under NFL rules.

At the time of the ejection, Metcalf had just one catch for two yards on four targets. He left the field without further comment and exited the locker room before media availability. It marked his third career disqualification since entering the league in 2019.

As a repeat offender with prior ejections and a two-game suspension last season for an altercation involving a fan, he faces the possibility of additional league discipline, including a fine or suspension.

The Steelers will prepare for their next game without knowing whether their top wideout will be available. The ejection added another costly distraction to an already difficult afternoon in Philadelphia.

articles.title: Lakers get encouraging Austin Reaves update as star nears return
articles.summary: Reaves has been ruled out for a fifth straight game on Monday against the Utah Jazz, but his return to the practice court is a positive sign for LA.
articles.body:
LOS ANGELES – Austin Reaves has been ruled out for a fifth straight game ahead of Monday's contest against the Utah Jazz , but there was an encouraging sight in El Segundo on Sunday afternoon.

Reaves stood at midcourt on the Los Angeles Lakers ' practice floor at UCLA Health Training Center, took off his gold practice jersey and conversed with assistant coach Greg St. Jean as he walked over to the left corner. From there, the 6-foot-5 shooting guard was running drills, coming off screens and working with two-way center Carson Cooper.

"We didn't do anything live, but he was a full participant," head coach JJ Redick said.

Redick went on to say that Reaves' practice day consisted mostly of "cleaning up some stuff" followed by two sets of defensive and offensive breakdowns before finishing the day by getting shots up.

The Lakers star has been sidelined since landing awkwardly on his left heel midway through the third quarter of their road win against the Milwaukee Bucks on Wednesday, Nov. 11. X-rays came back negative that night and both Reaves and team medical staff opted against further imaging.

He's been considered day-to-day with a left heel bone bruise and contusion since, though Redick said Sunday that Reaves has been making progress in his recovery.

"They're doing a great job of figuring out the most comfortable insert and the most comfortable shoe," he said. "Finding that right combination."

Jokić, Shai or Wemby? Ranking the NBA's 50 best players

Redick's insight is particularly valuable in this instance, considering he went through a similar injury himself when he suffered a bone bruise on the bottom of his heel in the last game of the regular season while playing with the Los Angeles Clippers .

"I had to play with it in the playoffs and was taking Toradol shots before the game. It was super painful," he said. "His is in a different spot, it's on the medial side so it's not on the bottom of the foot, but it's really just a comfort/pain issue."

The Lakers can't get Reaves back in the lineup soon enough. Quentin Grimes has had an impressive stretch stepping up in the Wichita State and Oklahoma product's absence, most notably a career-high 47-point game on 10 made 3s while leading the Lakers to an overtime comeback win over the Charlotte Hornets , their overall offense has suffered.

Luka Dončić, the early frontrunner for MVP, has struggled in particular the last two games and has looked downright fatigued at times to keep up his torrid start to the season. He's turned the ball over 20 times in the last three games. And collectively, the Lakers have shot the ball poorly. Dončić, Sandro Mamukelashvili and Jake LaRavia have all seen their 3-point percentages plummet over the last week after looking automatic from deep not long before then.

The stat that stands out the most to Redick: For the first 12 games, the Lakers had the top-rated halfcourt offense in the league. Reaves was on the floor for 70% of those possessions. articles.title: Dylan Larkin traded to Montreal Canadiens for goalie, package of picks
articles.summary: The Detroit Red Wings acquired goaltender Samuel Montenbeault in a package deal with the Montreal Canadiens for disgruntled ex-captain Dylan Larkin.
articles.body:
The divorce between the Detroit Red Wings and disgruntled former captain Dylan Larkin is finally complete.

Interim general manager Shawn Horcoff traded Larkin to the Montreal Canadiens on Sunday, Nov. 22, acquiring forwards Kirby Dach, Michigan Wolverines prospect Michael Hage, goaltender Samuel Montembeault, first-round picks in 2027 and 2028 and a second round pick in 2028 and a fourth-round pick in 2028.

Larkin is in Year 4 of an eight-year deal carrying an $8.7 million salary cap hit that is highly favorable in a league where the 2026-27 salary cap ceiling is $104 million. Larkin, 30, signed an eight-year, $69.6 million extension with the Wings on March 1, 2023.

Dylan Larkin, ex-Detroit Red Wings captain, Michigan native

Larkin had two goals and four assists in 10 games for the Wings this season, before leaving the team on Oct. 29. The Wings suspended Larkin without pay that same day , costing him $41,237.11 a day. Larkin's agent, Pat Brisson, told reporters, "Dylan's had enough of the situation." Sunday morning marked more than $1 million of salary forfeited back to the team.

Larkin's final goal in a Wings uniform came Oct. 26, tying the game late in the third period at Edmonton in an eventual thrilling shootout win. He didn't play again.

Larkin was soundly booed by his hometown fans when he was introduced during opening night Oct. 2 at Little Caesars Arena while out with an upper-body injury sustained in the offseason .

Larkin was again booed in his season debut Oct. 6 after missing the season's first two games, but turned jeers to cheers after scoring a goal and being named the game's first star.

Montreal fans at Bell Centre chanted "We want Larkin!" on Oct. 10, the most notable away crowd reaction to the saga.

When does Dylan Larkin return to Detroit?

Red Wings fans will have to wait until Feb. 18 to make their thoughts on the trade clear to Larkin again; that's Montreal's next visit to Little Caesars Arena, with another visit set for March 20.

Dylan Larkin history with Detroit Red Wings

News broke on June 4 that Larkin, who had a no-trade clause, had requested a trade after 11 seasons with his hometown Wings. Larkin is from nearby Waterford, attended the University of Michigan in Ann Arbor and had been the Wings' captain until he was stripped of the title after the trade request became public.

Larkin has gone 10 years without appearing in the NHL playoffs – the Wings own the NHL's longest playoff drought – and his gold-medal success at the 2026 Milano Olympics likely reminded him how fun it is to win important games.

He returned to Detroit from that experience, and watched as a Wings team that had been 10 points inside the playoff picture in late January lost its foothold and dropped out of contention, again.

Steve Yzerman, removed as GM in July , said shortly after the season he received a phone call from Larkin's agent informing him Larkin wanted to be traded. A week later, a list of teams Larkin would waive his no-trade clause for was provided.

Larkin's initial trade wish list – provided by his agent Brisson, who represented Horcoff during his NHL career in 2000-16 – was limited to three teams: Florida Panthers, Vegas Golden Knights and Minnesota Wild. The Panthers then traded with Ottawa for Brady Tkachuk , taking them out of the Larkin bidding.

"Dylan has five years remaining on his contract," Yzerman said June 27 after the NHL Draft. "My job as the manager of the Detroit Red Wings is always to do what is in the best interest of the Detroit Red Wings and I will act accordingly to that. I cannot make any guarantees or did not make any guarantees that that request could or would be met."

The list expanded in the fall to 10 teams to include the Dallas Stars, Washington Capitals, Carolina Hurricanes, Utah Mammoth, Tampa Bay Lightning, New Jersey Devils and Colorado Avalanche.

Horcoff said Sept. 16, one day after being named interim GM, that a rebuild was "out of the question," making the Larkin situation more difficult to resolve.

"We have too many good players in that lineup," Horcoff said. "We've been close. The last three years in a row, we've been really close. We're not looking backward, we're looking forward. We want to focus on what it's going to take for us to get over that hump."

But a Larkin deal finally came to fruition – while restricted free agent Simon Edvinsson bizarrely remains without a contract and wishes to be traded. (He must sign a contract by a 5 p.m. deadline on Dec. 1 or sit out the season in the NHL.)

Larkin now gets a chance to show what he can do elsewhere and return to the playoffs for the first time since 2016, his rookie year, while the Wings work to reshape their roster.

The Wings on Oct. 14 signed Alex DeBrincat to a seven-year, $91 million contract extension , the richest deal in franchise history.

articles.title: VP of Instant Replay addresses Parker Washington's non-touchdown catch
articles.summary: Following the Jaguars vs. Giants game, the VP of Instant Replay addressed Parker Washington's non-touchdown catch.
articles.body:
Early in the fourth quarter of the Jaguars vs. Giants game, it looked like Jacksonville wide receiver Parker Washington came down with a touchdown catch in the back of the end zone.

After initially bobbling the ball in tight coverage, Washington appeared to secure possession on the way to the ground while getting both feet in bounds.

However, the initial call on the field was incomplete. Liam Coen then challenged the play, but it was not overturned.

In the post-game pool report, Pat Leonard interviewed Vice President of Instant Replay Mark Butterworth, and asked about the non-touchdown catch.

"The ruling on the field was an incomplete pass," said Butterworth. "First, to overturn a call, we need clear and obvious video evidence to overturn the on-field ruling. It was determined that the receiver did not gain full control of the ball until he was out of bounds."

A follow-up question from Leonard asked for further clarification. "So, when his right foot touches the ground first, it's not determiend that he has control of the ball at that moment?" said Leonard.

To which Buttworth replied, "He needs to maintain control of the ball throughout the process of the catch."

When Washington contacted the ground, Butterworth deemed that the ball was still moving in his hands.

Instead of the touchdown making it a 20-13 game in favor of the Giants , the Jaguars had to settle for a field goal, keeping it a two-score game at 20-9. The Giants would win Sunday's matchup 23-18.

articles.title: Pierre LeBrun Reveals Stunning Dylan Larkin Trade Secret Kept Quiet for Months
articles.summary: Pierre LeBrun reveals Dylan Larkin was open to Montreal for months and explains Michael Hage's critical role in the Red Wings blockbuster trade.
articles.body:
The Dylan Larkin trade saga finally came to an end Sunday night when the Detroit Red Wings sent their former captain to the Montreal Canadiens in a blockbuster deal. But according to NHL insider Pierre LeBrun , there was a major secret being kept behind the scenes for months.

And it changes the way we look at how this entire situation unfolded.

Following the trade, LeBrun revealed that Larkin had actually been willing to accept a move to Montreal for more than two months. However, the Canadiens and Larkin's representatives reportedly agreed to keep that information quiet.

"So, it turns out Dylan Larkin was actually open to a trade to Montreal for more than two months," LeBrun wrote on X, according to the post provided. "But the Canadiens wanted to keep that quiet because they felt it would add an extra layer of noise that might hamper getting a deal done. And Larkin's camp agreed."

That's a fascinating revelation considering the months of speculation surrounding Larkin's approved trade destinations.

Michael Hage Was the Key to Getting the Deal Done

According to LeBrun, Montreal had been a legitimate possibility much longer than the public realized. However, the Canadiens still had to satisfy Detroit's asking price, which reportedly included one particularly important asset.

"Montreal agreeing to include Hage was a huge must for the Red Wings," LeBrun reported. "The deal started to come together and get serious on Friday."

That detail is especially interesting considering Hage had previously emerged as a potential centerpiece in a hypothetical deal between the two organizations.

Now, we know just how important the 20-year-old University of Michigan standout was to Detroit's negotiations.

According to the NHL's official trade announcement , the Red Wings received Hage, Kirby Dach, Samuel Montembeault, two conditional first-round picks, a second-round selection, and a fourth-round pick.

Montreal received Larkin, along with Detroit's 2027 third-round and 2028 second-round selections.

LeBrun's Revelation Raises New Questions

Perhaps the most interesting aspect of LeBrun's report is how it contrasts with the information available throughout the trade saga.

Earlier this month, reports indicated Larkin's camp was unwilling to expand his approved list , even as Montreal continued expressing interest.

Now, LeBrun's latest account suggests the Canadiens had privately received Larkin's blessing long before Sunday's announcement.

That doesn't necessarily mean the earlier reporting was inaccurate. It does, however, suggest there was considerably more happening behind the scenes than the public knew.

For Detroit, the biggest takeaway may be that interim general manager Shawn Horcoff held firm on acquiring Hage rather than settling for a package without the highly regarded prospect.

And if LeBrun's timeline is accurate, a trade saga that appeared to drag on for months may have ultimately come down to one critical breakthrough on Friday.

The Canadiens finally agreed to include Michael Hage, and two days later, Dylan Larkin was on his way to Montreal.

articles.title: Jalen Smith doing it all as Bulls attempts to right ship
articles.summary: The Chicago Bulls are looking to bounce back. They just went on an eight-game losing streak. Plus, they lost Caleb Wilson to a broken hand for at least six w...
articles.body:
The Chicago Bulls are looking to bounce back. They just went on an eight-game losing streak. Plus, they lost Caleb Wilson to a broken hand for at least six weeks.

On Sunday, they welcomed the Denver Nuggets to complete a week in which they played four games. With Nic Claxton out with an illness , Jalen Smith once again filled in at center. And it was a good thing, even though he was listed as probable due to illness himself.

He was virtually all over the floor. Smith took good shots, went for rebounds, and showed pure versatility. All of which came together in one sequence in the 2nd quarter. At the 7:53 mark, Tre Jones went for the 3-pointer, but missed. Smith grabbed the rebound and kicked it back out to Jones. Jones pumped-faked it before finding the open Buddy Hield on the wing. Hield penetrated the lane, dished it to Smith, who then slammed it down with authority.

He finished the half with 15 points and went 6-for-7 from the field. In Claxton's absence, Smith has emerged as a major catalyst at center.

Altogether, he is averaging 13.4 points and 7.9 rebounds per game while shooting 52.8% from the field. Additionally, Smith has scored in double figures in 11 games this season. His highest-scoring game came on November 11 against the San Antonio Spurs, when he finished with 23 points.

Meanwhile, Smith has bounced back from injury scares , usually stemming from aggressive play. Chicago trailed Denver 72-70 at the half.

articles.title: Justin Herbert enters concussion protocol after Chargers’ Week 11 loss to Jets
articles.summary: Justin Herbert and the Los Angeles Chargers were sent crashing back to earth after losing to the New York Jets, 27-24, at SoFi Stadium on Sunday. All the hi...
articles.body:
Justin Herbert and the Los Angeles Chargers were sent crashing back to earth after losing to the New York Jets, 27-24 , at SoFi Stadium on Sunday.

All the high from the Chargers' win over the Baltimore Ravens in Week 10 was erased, and it could be more costly, as Herbert was placed in concussion protocol. He played the entire game without exiting for a sideline evaluation. The Chargers have not specified the exact play on which he got hurt.

The 28-year-old quarterback did not face the media , as noted by KTLA's Hayley Elwood.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

"Justin Herbert is in the concussion protocol per Chargers PR. He will not be speaking postgame," wrote Elwood on X.

Herbert absorbed significant punishment against the Jets, taking six sacks and eight hits. He suffered a smack to the facemask from David Bailey in the second quarter, which drew a roughing-the-passer call.

The two-time Pro Bowler threw 15-of-21 for 131 yards and two touchdowns. He also scored on a short rush to end the first half.

The Chargers remained winless at home and fell to 1-9. The Jets, meanwhile, broke their five-game losing streak to the Chargers and improved to 3-8.

The much-hyped pairing of Herbert and Mike McDaniel has not worked, and Los Angeles is in danger of missing the playoffs for the second time in four years.

If Herbert is unable to clear the concussion protocol before Week 12 against the New England Patriots, DJ Uiagalelei is next in line to start, with Trey Lance out with a groin injury and Jake Browning on the practice squad.

articles.title: Five takeaways from UCLA basketball's mauling the Delaware Blue Hens
articles.summary: Five takeaways from the No. 7 UCLA Bruins 85-48 win against the Delaware Blue Hens at the Pauley Pavilion on Sunday.
articles.body:
The No. 7 UCLA Bruins men's basketball team decimated the Delaware Blue Hens with an 85-48 win at the Pauley Pavilion on Sunday.

The win concludes the Bruins five game homestand as UCLA extended their win streak to six games. The Bruins learned from their previous games and Delaware was never able to hold the lead, as UCLA continued to pile on points and blow the Blue Hens out. Here were five takeaways from their win.

The Bruins have been monsters when they run to the basket and this game was no different. In fact, this was UCLA's best game in the paint with a monstrous 52-points. The Bruins also had a good game from the field by shooting 55% and 28% from beyond the arc. That's an incredibly dangerous offense that tore through Delaware's defense and would lead to the Bruins creating a 41-point lead at one point in the game.

UCLA continued to have new players shine bright for them on a game-in and game-out basis. This time it was sophomore center Filip Jovic, who came off the bench and led the game with 17 points in his 19 minutes of play. Jovic made 7-of-8 field goal attempts, but also snagged six rebounds and had two assists.

Bruins sophomore guard Jaylen Petty was out of the lineup this game and senior center Xavier Booker returned to the starting lineup. In his return, Booker scored 10 points, grabbed four rebounds, one assist and three steals to propel his team to a monstrous lead. Booker's three steals were tied for the most of the game along with freshman forward Joe Philon III.

UCLA's defense has continued to be a focal point of the team this year with 11 steals to take complete control of the game. On top of that, the Bruins forced 11 more turnovers against the Blue Hens and scored 27 points off of the 22 turnovers. Defense opens up the offense and Delaware experienced the formula the Bruins use to win games first hand.

The Bruins had a 19-point lead heading into halftime and they didn't leave this game up to chance. UCLA silenced Delaware's offense to begin the second half and swiftly made it a blowout. It seems like the Bruins learned that they can't play with their food and defense is necessary for the entirety of the game. With the win, the Bruins are 6-0 and are in pretty good shape as they inch closer towards conference play.

articles.title: 49ers’ Colton McKivitz suffers horrifying leg injury in Mexico City

articles.body:
San Francisco 49ers offensive lineman Colton McKivitz suffered a gruesome injury during Sunday's game against the Minnesota Vikings in Mexico City.

McKivitz — who had played in 77 straight games entering the game — seemed to snap his lower leg while blocking during a play.

The broadcast showed his left foot seemingly twisted to the side before cutting to a timeout. When they returned, many 49ers players were visibly shaken up and taking a knee.

It is way too early to tell exactly what happened to the 30-year-old lineman. But there's no doubt that this was a very serious injury.

This is a tough loss for the 49ers, who have one of the league's best offensive lines.

But the hope right now is that McKivitz's injury isn't as bad as it looked.

There is surely more to come on his injury's severity.
