articles.title: Magic fall flat, trail entire night in loss to Wizards
articles.summary: The Magic fell behind by as many as 25 points and never led against the Wizards on Sunday night to go 1-1 on their two-game weekend road trip. With all five...
articles.body:
The Magic fell behind by as many as 25 points and never led against the Wizards on Sunday night to go 1-1 on their two-game weekend road trip.

With all five members of its starting lineup finishing in double figures, including five-time All-NBA big man Anthony Davis (22 points), Washington cruised to its third straight victory, 116-96, over Orlando inside Capital One Arena.

The Magic had a hard time keeping up with the Wizards from distance, an area of the court where Washington knocked down 56% of its 3-point shots and held Orlando to just 31% shooting on the other end.

It's the second win for Washington over Orlando this month. The Magic lost to the Wizards by nine points at home on Nov. 2, and the sides will face each other a third time in November on Saturday. The sides won't see each other again until much later in the season on April 3 for their fourth and final regular-season meeting as Southeast Division opponents.

Washington (7-11) did a solid job slowing down Magic forward Franz Wagner, who had scored 30-plus points in five of the past seven games. Wagner was limited to 16 points in the loss while teammate Jalen Suggs missed all six of his 3-point attempts to score just nine points in 22 minutes of action.

The Magic (7-9) will look to regroup at home when they host the Pistons in a big NBA Cup game on Tuesday night at Kia Center.

The Magic lacked a sense of urgency when the Wizards scored the first 11 points of the game. It took three minutes of action for Orlando to get on the board after back-to-back layups from Franz Wagner.

Washington had success pushing the ball in transition and from beyond the arc in the opening frame. The Wizards held an 11-0 advantage in fast break points and shot 6 for 11 from 3-point by the end of the first quarter.

Meanwhile, the Magic went 3 for 14 from distance in the first quarter and was outrebounded 15-7 to fall behind by 17 points, 38-21, after the opening 12 minutes of the game.

Washington entered Sunday's game shooting 31.9% from beyond the arc, which marked the third-worst 3-point percentage in the league.

But against the Magic, the Wizards could hardly miss from distance.

Orlando often failed to closeout on defense to open shooters on the perimeter and the Wizards made them pay for the disfunction. Through three quarters alone, Washington tied its season-high for 3-pointers made in a game with 18.

The Wizards finished 22 for 39 from 3-point range and had seven different players hit from distance, including guard Bilal Coulibaly who made four. Coulibaly had made a total of six 3-pointers in his first 16 games played this season.

On the other end of the floor, the Magic finished 12 for 39 from 3-point range with both reserves Nikola Vucevic and Jevon Carter both shooting 1 for 4 on the perimeter. Desmond Bane (17 points) shot 3 for 8 from 3 in 33 minutes.

One of the few bright spots for the Magic on Sunday night was the play of third-year forward Tristan da Silva.

After scoring just six points at Brooklyn on Friday night, da Silva bounced back in a major way with 18 points in 27 minutes off the bench.

Da Silva knocked down a team-high four 3-pointers when he shot 6 for 10 from the field and added three rebounds.

articles.title: SEC Rivalry Week Schedule Sets Up a Dramatic Finish With Plenty at Stake
articles.summary: BIRMINGHAM, Ala. — The Southeastern Conference has saved some of its most anticipated matchups for last. Rivalry Week arrives Friday, Nov. 27, with conferenc...
articles.body:
BIRMINGHAM, Ala. — The Southeastern Conference has saved some of its most anticipated matchups for last.

Rivalry Week arrives Friday, Nov. 27, with conference championship implications, postseason positioning and decades of bad blood sharing the spotlight.

Georgia has already secured its place in the SEC Championship Game. However, Alabama, Tennessee and Texas still have unfinished business.

Meanwhile, several other programs have an opportunity to close their seasons with bragging rights that last considerably longer than one Saturday.

South Carolina-Clemson's exact kickoff time and television assignment remain among the options listed by the conference.

Texas visits Texas A&M on Friday night, giving the Longhorns the first opportunity to influence the SEC Championship Game race.

A victory would improve Texas to 7-2 in conference play and place pressure on Alabama and Tennessee entering Saturday.

However, a loss would eliminate the Longhorns from contention for the conference title game.

Earlier Friday, Ole Miss hosts Mississippi State in the Egg Bowl. Florida also travels to Tallahassee for its annual meeting with Florida State.

Georgia hosts Georgia Tech in Clean, Old-Fashioned Hate, although the Bulldogs have already completed their SEC schedule.

Meanwhile, Tennessee visits Vanderbilt before Alabama hosts Auburn in the Iron Bowl.

Those two games could determine which team joins Georgia in Atlanta on Dec. 5.

Elsewhere, Oklahoma travels to Missouri, South Carolina visits Clemson and Kentucky hosts Louisville.

The regular season has produced plenty of surprises. Nevertheless, Rivalry Week has a way of making everything that happened before it feel like an opening act.

For the SEC, the final weekend promises more than bragging rights. It will help determine the conference's championship matchup and shape its playoff representation.
